items.title: Nasdaq ends October with worst day since June
items.what: Weak Intel and Amazon results fed doubts about AI spending. Nasdaq fell 2.9% and chip stocks sank, making October its worst month since March 2025.

items.title: CoreWeave and Nebius each fall more than 10%
items.what: AI cloud renters were hit hardest as investors fretted over their debt and big customers' spending, leaving both stocks down roughly a third in October.

items.title: SoftBank drops nearly 7% as Asian chip stocks tumble
items.what: SoftBank, a key funder of OpenAI, fell sharply in Tokyo as the Amazon and Intel results hit AI-linked stocks across Asia.

items.title: Chip stocks tumble after Intel and Amazon results
items.what: Chipmakers from AMD to Micron, Broadcom and Nvidia sold off as Intel's and Amazon's results soured the mood on AI hardware.

items.title: Nasdaq drops over 2% to a near three-month low
items.what: Amazon and Intel deepened fears that AI building costs won't pay off soon; big tech stocks are on track to lose $2T+ in October.

items.title: Intel crashes about 30%, heading for its worst day ever
items.what: Intel warned of weak PC demand, factory setbacks and burning cash this year, so investors dumped the stock.

items.title: Amazon's AI spending pushes its yearly cash flow to -$42B
items.what: AWS cloud sales grew 39%, but data-center spending was so heavy that Amazon spent $42B more cash than it took in over a year.

items.title: Microsoft borrows $25 billion in a giant bond sale
items.what: Even cash-rich Microsoft is borrowing $25B from bond investors, adding to Big Tech's fast-growing debt as AI spending climbs.

items.title: Alphabet has its worst day ever, losing ~$482B
items.what: Google's stock fell 12.6% after search growth slowed and AI spending drained cash, erasing about $482B of value in one day.

items.title: Nvidia in talks to back Nscale's debt for Anthropic site
items.what: Nvidia may co-sign billions of Nscale borrowing for a West Virginia campus Anthropic plans to use; nothing is signed yet.

items.title: Google Cloud doubles, but AI spending turns cash flow negative
items.what: Google Cloud sales jumped 103%, yet $51B of quarterly data-center spending left Alphabet $9.1B short on cash.

items.title: Microsoft's Azure cloud grows 48%, beating forecasts
items.what: Strong demand for Microsoft's AI cloud lifted quarterly sales to $92B, a sign big customers are still paying up for AI.

items.title: Microsoft spends less than planned as outside capacity arrives late
items.what: Delayed deliveries kept Microsoft's AI spending at $45B versus $51B expected, and chip-renters like CoreWeave and Nebius fell about 6%.

items.title: Nvidia puts $3B into Meta's new stock sale
items.what: A chip supplier is now buying a slice of its customer, sending fresh equity money from Nvidia to Meta.

items.title: Meta plans to sell up to $95B of new stock for AI
items.what: Meta will sell $35B of new shares now and up to $60B more from 2027 to pay for AI data centers, diluting current owners.

items.title: Anthropic files to go public on Nasdaq as 'ANT'
items.what: Anthropic's filing shows $16.3B of first-half sales, about 14 times a year earlier, opening a top AI lab to public investors.

items.title: SpaceX lines up a $40B deal to lease Nvidia chips
items.what: Apollo would buy Nvidia's newest AI chips and rent them to SpaceX for about five years, a giant order landing in 2027.

items.title: AI chip-renters CoreWeave and Nebius are down 30%+ this month
items.what: After Musk's warning these rental firms fell again, and their bonds hit record lows as lenders grew more nervous.

items.title: Musk warns 200+ AI cloud startups could fail as lending dries up
items.what: Musk said lenders have nearly stopped funding AI chip-rental firms without other income, so most will fail or be merged.

items.title: Nasdaq falls 2.6%, its worst day since June, as Meta sinks
items.what: Meta lost 7% and chip stocks dropped nearly 7% as investors doubted how much more AI spending can pay off.

items.title: SoftBank has now lost half its value since June
items.what: Big OpenAI backer SoftBank fell another 6.9% on AI debt fears, and the cost of insuring its debt hit a near four-year high.

items.title: OpenAI nears $30B raise at $1.25T value
items.what: OpenAI wants signed commitments within about a week for a bridge round before a likely 2027 IPO, led by UAE investors and Coatue.

items.title: Meta burns cash for the first time since 2012
items.what: Meta poured $35B into AI building in one quarter, more than its business brought in, leaving it about $2B short.

items.title: SpaceX sales jump 161% as its AI business booms
items.what: Renting AI computing power to Anthropic and Google helped SpaceX grow revenue to $14.6B and swing to a $4.4B profit.

items.title: Nasdaq has its worst week since June on AI debt fears
items.what: Worry that AI firms borrowed too much hit tech stocks; CoreWeave lost a quarter of its value in a single week.

items.title: Chip stocks fall eight days straight, longest streak since 2008
items.what: Micron, AMD, Broadcom and Intel each dropped about 5% Friday as investors pulled money out of AI hardware bets.

items.title: Nvidia's Huang defends CoreWeave and its stock bounces 5.9%
items.what: Nvidia's CEO said CoreWeave gets stronger daily and its borrowing costs are falling, briefly calming fears about its debt.

items.title: Gartner: most AI cloud renters won't survive on their own
items.what: Gartner expects AI data-center revenue to lag building costs, so 80% of chip-rental firms may lose independence by 2030.

items.title: Cost of insuring against AI company defaults hits records
items.what: Markets now imply roughly a 63% chance CoreWeave defaults within five years; protection on Oracle, SoftBank and Big Tech debt also rose.

items.title: TSMC's profit jumps 69% as chip orders keep pouring in
items.what: TSMC took in $46.7B last quarter and forecast more for next quarter, a sign demand for its most advanced chips is still strong.

items.title: CoreWeave's bonds trade at distress levels, near 15% yields
items.what: Bond investors now demand about 15% a year to hold CoreWeave's debt, showing doubt it can comfortably repay; its stock fell 16%.

items.title: Oracle sinks 9% as AI borrowing fears spread
items.what: Oracle borrowed heavily to build data centers, so CoreWeave's bond scare dragged it down along with Dell, AMD and smaller AI clouds.

items.title: Hot inflation report raises odds of interest-rate hikes
items.what: Prices rose 3.7% from a year ago, so borrowing may get pricier, bad news for AI firms paying for data centers with debt.

items.title: Anthropic's quarterly revenue hits $16.8B, and it turns a profit
items.what: Anthropic told investors sales jumped to $16.8B last quarter with a profit, rare proof that an AI lab can make money.

items.title: Broadcom's CEO compares AI investors to casino gamblers
items.what: Though Broadcom expects AI chip sales to reach $230B by 2028, its CEO warned that access to money could become AI's biggest limit.

items.title: OpenAI's sales pace is about $50B a year, below earlier reports
items.what: OpenAI's yearly revenue pace is near $50B, not the nearly $70B reported weeks earlier, once counted more like Anthropic's.

items.title: Nasdaq closes at a record high before October's slide
items.what: Tech stocks peaked with the Nasdaq near 27,600; AI debt and spending worries erased about 6% within three weeks.

items.title: SoftBank sends OpenAI another $10B, finishing a $30B pledge
items.what: SoftBank's total bet on OpenAI reaches $64.6B for about 13% ownership, paid partly with money it raised by selling bonds.
